title: Freedom extended to necessary acts is taken in a broader sense
source_text: IX. Quum autem libertas extenditur ad actus necessarios atque immutabiles, fatentur illam latiori significatione sumi; libertatem vero strictius acceptam versari tantum circa contingentia, & quae possunt sic, vel secus se habere.
pass_a_gloss: But when liberty is extended to necessary and immutable acts, they confess that it is taken in a wider signification; but that liberty more strictly accepted is concerned only with contingent things, and those which can be so, or otherwise.
pass_b_english: They admit that when freedom is stretched to cover acts that are necessary and unchangeable, the word is being used in a broader sense.
Taken more strictly, freedom deals only with what is contingent: with what may turn out one way or the other.

choices.why: Kept as in the preceding locus on free choice in general, so the Roman and Reformed accounts are compared in one vocabulary.
